questions.q: According to the summary, what has driven the widening gap between the wealthy and everyone else in the US?
a: Deliberate policy choices made by rich people and corporations
Random economic cycles that no one could control
A steady decline in the number of available jobs
Cultural differences between generations of workers
questions.why: The opening argument says income inequality is not an accident but the result of intentional policies that concentrate power and money.

questions.q: What does the summary say over-privatization does to governments?
a: It makes them rely on the financial industry for much of their revenue
It makes them more efficient at serving ordinary citizens
It removes private influence from public services entirely
It gives working-class families more bargaining power
questions.why: Lesson 1 explains that as services are privatized, governments depend on finance for revenue while finance depends on government for stability.

questions.q: What happened to the middle class as government spending on families fell?
a: It shrank while corporations outsourced jobs to cheaper countries
It grew steadily as taxes on the wealthy were raised
It stayed the same but worked fewer hours each week
It moved into better-paid manufacturing jobs at home
questions.why: Lesson 2 ties the shrinking middle class to lower spending on families and to companies moving work to low-income countries.

questions.q: Why does the summary say Congress ignores most Americans who want universal health care?
a: It answers to lobbyists from powerful insurance companies
It is legally required to follow corporate shareholders
Most voters have stopped supporting the idea
The courts have blocked every health care vote
questions.why: Lesson 3 uses universal health care as an example of Congress serving lobbyists rather than the majority of citizens.

questions.q: How do corporations keep their influence over government, according to the summary?
a: Through campaign contributions and lawsuits against critics
By refusing to pay any taxes at all
By running their own candidates in elections
By withdrawing from global markets entirely
questions.why: Lesson 3 describes lobbying through campaign money and legal action against anyone who challenges corporate interests.
